threat: A rogue component impersonates API gateway and WAF to its callers or data stores, or API gateway and WAF accepts a caller it has not properly identified.
mitigation: Give API gateway and WAF its own workload identity (managed identity, mTLS certificate or signed service token); verify the identity of every caller and every downstream service it talks to; never share credentials between components.

threat: Input to API gateway and WAF is crafted to change its behaviour (injection, parameter manipulation, business-logic abuse) or its code and configuration are modified without authorisation.
mitigation: Validate and encode all input at the boundary of API gateway and WAF; use parameterised queries and safe APIs; sign or hash deployed artefacts; manage configuration as code with reviewed changes.

threat: Actions performed through API gateway and WAF cannot be attributed to a user or a calling system afterwards.
mitigation: Emit audit events from API gateway and WAF for authentication, authorisation decisions and data changes, including the caller identity and a correlation ID; forward them to central, append-only logging.

threat: API gateway and WAF reveals more than it should: verbose errors, debug endpoints, secrets in configuration, or responses containing data the caller is not entitled to see.
mitigation: Return generic error messages from API gateway and WAF; disable debug features in production; keep secrets in a vault, not in code or environment files; filter responses to the minimum fields the caller needs.

threat: API gateway and WAF is overwhelmed or crashed by a flood of requests, expensive operations or malformed input, making the service unavailable.
mitigation: Rate-limit and size-limit requests to API gateway and WAF; set time-outs on every downstream call; autoscale with an upper bound; test failure modes; monitor saturation and alert.

threat: A caller of API gateway and WAF performs an action or reaches data beyond its role, or API gateway and WAF itself runs with more privilege than its function needs.
mitigation: Enforce authorisation on every request inside API gateway and WAF (object level and function level); run API gateway and WAF under a least-privilege identity; separate administrative interfaces from user-facing ones.

threat: Changes to Customer and order database cannot be traced to who or what made them.
mitigation: Enable change auditing on Customer and order database (who, what, when); protect the audit trail separately from the data.

threat: Data held in Customer and order database is read by someone who should not see it: exposed storage, stolen backup, over-broad query, or leakage through logs and exports.
mitigation: Encrypt Customer and order database at rest with managed keys; limit read access per role; mask or tokenise sensitive fields; control exports and backups; delete data when it is no longer needed.

threat: Customer and order database becomes unavailable or is filled up — ransomware, deletion, quota exhaustion, corrupted replica.
mitigation: Back up Customer and order database regularly and test restores; use redundancy appropriate to its criticality; monitor capacity; isolate backups from production credentials.
